aboutMore: Further particulars. My mother works nights in the hospital laundry, 11 to 7, so I rise at 6:30 and prepare her breakfast (one egg, toast, tea in the Ultimania mug) before she arrives. This is not a side quest. It is the main one. I am also a Library Aide, fourth period, with a lanyard (it says STAFF) and a cart. I know the Dewey Decimal System well enough to find any book in 40 seconds, including the ones nobody has ever checked out. My cousin Dale (8) believes I am a king. I have not corrected him. The Reunion remains scheduled.

blog.title: THE REUNION: LOGISTICS MEMO (DRAFT 3)
blog.body: DATE: my birthday, in August. VENUE: the basement (cleared; the treadmill has been covered with a cape). DURATION: 3 hours, 14 minutes of which are 'the lore.' GUEST LIST (7 invited): usagi (confirmed, bringing pocky), wes (confirmed, bringing a PS1 and one CRT 'for ambiance'), kevin (confirmed, 'after Tilt'), darkangel (confirmed, glitter candles, 11:11), dave (maybe), my cousin Dale (confirmed; he is 8; he did not have a vote), my mother (confirmed; she lives here). CAKE: my mother is making it. She asked what a meteor is shaped like. I said 'a rock with ambition.' She said 'so a potato.' It will be a potato. I will cherish the potato. BALLOONS: 9, silver. I do not know why nine. It seemed correct. NOTE: if five attend, it is a party. If one attends, it is a meeting. I would like a party. I will accept a meeting.

blog.title: Part 0: The Mother Problem (not posted to the series)
blog.body: The series contains 40 parts about a mother who was, by any measure, a catastrophe. This is Part 0. It is not in the series. My own mother works in the hospital laundry from 11 PM to 7 AM, folding sheets that belong to strangers who are sick. She comes home at 7:10. At 6:30 I am awake. I make one egg, toast and tea. I put the tea in the Ultimania mug because the mug is large and tea holds heat. She sits. She says 'what's the plot today.' I tell her one scene. She nods and eats. Then she sleeps, and I go to school. This is the only part of my day with no yardstick in it. I have not told the Lifestream. I am telling you. It is the best-written thing in my life and I did not write it. She did. Part 41 will be about her. It will be five pages. (I have been told the limit.)

blog.title: Library Aide (the cart is a vehicle)
blog.body: Fourth period I am a Library Aide. The librarian, Ms. Gerber, handed me a lanyard on the first day of school. It says STAFF. I have never been trusted with a word on a lanyard. My duties: shelving, the cart, and finding books for people who say 'it's blue, I think.' I know the Dewey Decimal System well enough to locate any book in 40 seconds, including books no one has ever checked out. Today a freshman asked for 'a book about a sad boy and a dog.' I returned in 38 seconds with Old Yeller. It was the wrong book. He wanted Where the Red Fern Grows. I returned with that in 51 seconds and the lanyard seemed to hum. The cart has a loose wheel that sings in the key of F. I consider this correct. Ms. Gerber says I walk the aisles 'like I'm heading into battle.' I said the battle is alphabetization. She laughed. A real laugh. I wrote it down.

blog.title: The Gold Chocobo: A 14-Hour Love Story
blog.body: It took 14 hours across three Sundays. The breeding chart is on a legal pad, with arrows, and the arrows have footnotes. I will not describe the footnotes. On the third Sunday, at 6:12 PM, the bird turned gold, and I made a sound my mother described from the kitchen as 'a kettle having feelings.' I named the bird Zack. I know. Crisis Core is not out. I am ALREADY emotional. I rode Zack across the plains for one hour with the sound off. I did not fight anything. I did not collect anything. I only rode. The gold chocobo can cross mountains. I did not need to cross a mountain. I crossed one anyway. It was the most peaceful hour of my week. I have since reset the file to do it again. A man must be allowed one hobby that ends in a bird.

survey.title: THE OFFICIAL SOLDIER APTITUDE QUESTIONNAIRE (self-administered)
qa: Name:
Sephiroth. (The others are pretenders.) My mother calls me 'Seph.' I permit this.
Occupation:
Library Aide, fourth period. Lanyard: STAFF. Also: the one who does the dishes.
Weapon of choice:
A yardstick with electrical tape. Secondary: a 12-inch ruler. Tertiary: eye contact.
Breakfast:
I do not eat breakfast. I MAKE breakfast. For someone else. At 6:30.
Pets:
None. My aunt has a beagle named Nanaki. He is unaware of the weight of his name.
Favorite Dewey number:
398.2. Folk tales. It is where the myths live. It has the best shelf in the building.
Biggest fear:
Being asked for a 'short summary.' I have never given one. My mother has asked twice. I gave her the long one. She listened to all of it.
Last time you laughed:
Ms. Gerber laughed at my alphabetization joke. I was so surprised I dropped a card. A real laugh. I wrote it down.
Something you are secretly good at:
Spelling. I placed second in the county bee in sixth grade. The word was 'chrysanthemum.' I was off by one letter. I do not speak of it. (I speak of it.)
Who do you call when you are sad:
My cousin Dale, age 8. He asks 'are you being a sad king.' I say yes. He says 'it's ok, kings are sad, here's a joke,' and the joke is always about a hot dog. It works.
Favorite thing about the library:
The sound it makes at 3:10 when everyone has left. It is the sound of 40,000 books exhaling. I stay ten more minutes. Ms. Gerber pretends not to notice.
One regret:
That I did not bring the yardstick to the dentist. I was alone. I felt exposed.
Describe yourself in one sentence:
I am a 16-year-old who makes eggs at 6:30 in the morning and tells his mother one scene of a video game, and I would not trade that for all the Mako in the Planet.

dms: {you}, a report. my cousin dale, age 8, asked me today whether i am real. i said 'i am as real as your dentist.' he said 'ok.' he left satisfied. i am unsure whether i won.
i have purchased the longer coat. $6.50. it has a stain in the shape of a small continent. i have decided it is the Northern Crater. i wear it with the stain facing inward, for mystery.

the library cart's wheel sings in the key of F. i have confirmed this with a tuning fork from the band room. a clarinet girl lent it to me and asked no questions. she is an ally. i will not be oiling the wheel.

{you}, i have a theory about malten's 'Why do I create?' it is one sentence. 'because the alternative is standing at the top of a stairwell with a yardstick.' i find this sufficient. it does not have a part number. that is how you know it is real.

wes has mailed me a CRT. one. for ambiance. it is 19 inches. i carried it up the stairs. my arms hurt. the yardstick is jealous. the television now plays the opening of FF7 on a loop with the sound off. the silence is perfect.
a question, with no yardstick in my hand. do you think anyone will come to the Reunion. i have four confirmed. i have nine balloons. a number is fine. i accept a number.
the gold chocobo is named zack. i know. i will not discuss it. he is a good bird. he crossed a mountain tonight with the sound off. that is all.

ms gerber has asked me to build the library's banned books display. i made a card for the Ultimania. she said it is not banned. i said it should be, for its power. she wrote 'not banned' on a sticky note and put it on my forehead. i am keeping it.

my mother asked me to teach her 'the game with the swords.' she said 'i want to see why you made breakfast about it.' i handed her the controller. she reached the part with the flowers and put it down and said 'oh, honey.' i have never been so well understood. she is on disc 2.
repliesExtra: I have read this twice, once for content and once for tone. Both were acceptable.
A fair statement. I will consider it on the walk to the stairwell. I consider everything there.
I would respond at length, but fourth period begins shortly and the cart does not shelve itself.
You write plainly. It is a rare gift. My own essays are 40 parts. I envy you.
My mother would react to this with 'oh, honey.' I am borrowing it. Oh, honey.
I accept this as a gift and file it under 398.2, with the other things that are true.
An unexpected kindness. I must sit with it on the top step of the stairwell. I will return shortly. Do not wait.
Understood. This is the sort of thing one says before a Reunion.
Noted. It has been entered into the Lifestream, beside the cake incident.
I have no lore for this. I have only gratitude. It is a new feeling. I am taking notes.

sephiroth's mother has hemmed the new coat's sleeves so he can raise an arm without looking like a bat. she did not ask why. the stairwell has never been so well dressed.

sephiroth has stayed 10 minutes after the library closed again. ms gerber says the quiet at 3:10 is 'a gift.' he agrees. the cart stayed too. it is a good cart.

Sephiroth, I have re-sorted you. Library Aide is a Ravenclaw job. You are a Slytherin with a Ravenclaw lanyard, which is a very rare combination. It would have confused the Hat. It would also have been interested. - Maddie

sephiroth-kun!! the draft of part 41 (the FIVE page one about your mom) was handed to me in room 204 and i had to go lie down. it's the best thing you have ever written. i said so out loud. the pocky is in the mail. ganbatte!!
seph the CRT. you carried a 19 incher up a staircase and did NOT drop it. that's a tech skill AND a strength skill. i'm proud. the ps1 is in the mail. be gentle with the disc 2 (i know you are)

gary: gary i saw the footnote in your FF7 FAQ: 'See also xXSephirothXx, Part 7 (disputed).' i have read it 9 times. it is the highest honor a FAQ has ever bestowed on a man. i will cite you in return. [6.4b]. i will not be correcting Lucrecia. (i will be correcting Lucrecia. in Part 9.)

gary you have corrected my section numbering 11 times. i have, in turn, corrected your use of 'its' in section 9. we are even. we are colleagues. i propose a co-authored 40 part series on the Jenova problem. you do the footnotes. i will do the grief. also: the ASCII Cloud in v1.07 is flawless. his hair is exactly correct.
rick: rick i do not play World of Warcraft. i have read of it. you lead a guild called Overtime with a spreadsheet named DKP_FINAL_v9_USE_THIS_ONE. it is the most honest form of government i have encountered. you also stock the cereal aisle at night with care. a king with a pallet jack. i would serve under you. (i would not serve. i would consult.)

rick thank you for Lore Keeper. i have written it on the inside of the coat. Terry has been informed. you clock out at 6:30. i rise at 6:30. we pass at dawn, like two shifts. when a raid fails, say 'this is not the end' in a calm voice. it is what the Lifestream would say.
maddie: maddie your sorting me as a Slytherin was acceptable. your claim that i 'cite myself 12 times' was a slander of one. i checked. it is 11. please issue a correction. (peer review accepted. i have sent Parts 1 through 5. do not read Parts 6 through 33. they are for me.)

maddie i have begun reading 'The Case for Severus Snape.' Part 4 is superb. he is not a villain. he is a man who loved too quietly. i see him. i have a lanyard. we have much in common. do not tell the Hat.
leo: leo i have seen your corkboard. 312 pushpins. 214 feet of string. an index card for every character. i find the red thread (the unexplained) the most moving. it is the most accurate Jenova plot map i have ever seen. we should discuss over a legal pad. we live in the same city. we may be on the same hallway.

leo you say 'the numbers' are cursed. i have a number as well: 7. it was on the wall in Nibelheim. it is on my locker. your locker is 42. we are not neighbors. we are on opposite ends of the building. but we are connected by a very long string. (i have not seen the string. i believe in the string.)
